newsitem.title: GERMANY: German police see "personal motive" for church bomb.
newsitem.headline: German police see "personal motive" for church bomb.

text.p: German police said on Thursday a 49-year-old woman who killed herself and two other people in a Christmas Eve church bomb attack had been undergoing psychiatric treatment and was most probably driven by "personal motives".
A police spokesman told Reuters the woman had been separated for the last year from her husband. He lived with their nine-year-old daughter in Frankfurt.
The three had lived together in the Frankfurt district of Sindlingen where the attack took place during the 1980s, police said.
"I believe her motives were personal," said Frankfurt police spokesman Peter Borchardt. "A political motive can be ruled out."

The suicide bomber was blown to pieces at a midnight Protestant church service by the blast caused by two hand grenades strapped to her abdomen. She was identified after police published a photograph of her severed head.

Police inspecting her flat in the outlying town of Usingen have not found a suicide note. But Borchardt said investigators believe the woman, who apparently took public transport to the church, did not intend to kill many people.
"Apparently she underestimated the effects the hand grenades would have," Borchardt said.
The woman, whom police did not name out of respect for her family, detonated two hand grenades strapped to her abdomen. Two women sitting next to her at the midnight church service were killed.
She was from Roedelheim, a Frankfurt district a few kilometres (miles) from the South Sindlingen Protestant church she attacked, but had been living in the town of Usingen north of Frankfurt.
Thirteen other worshippers, including a 12-year-old girl, were injured when the blast sent shrapnel, oily black smoke and bits of smashed pews flying through the Protestant church, police said.
